neighbours.label: Words for holding the top rank among powers: ' dominant', ' supremacy', hegemony, pre-eminent, ' leadership' in talk of states and rivals. The pole also fires on ' city' in the planning ideals 'garden city' / 'world city', which is listed here and not tested.
fire: For two centuries Spain was the dominant power in the western Mediterranean.
Rome's naval supremacy was sealed after the defeat of Carthage.
Historians date the end of Dutch commercial dominance to the 1670s.
The treaty confirmed Prussia as the dominant state in northern Germany.
Athens lost its supremacy over the league within a generation.
By 1900 the firm had become the dominant producer of steel rails.
Venice fought for decades to keep its supremacy in the spice trade.
The dynasty's dominance over the steppe tribes did not last.
quiet: For two centuries Spain traded with ports in the western Mediterranean.
Rome's navy was rebuilt after the defeat of Carthage.
Historians date the end of Dutch tulip speculation to the 1630s.
The treaty confirmed the border between Prussia and Denmark.
Athens lost many ships to storms within a generation.
By 1900 the firm had opened a second mill for steel rails.
Venice fought for decades against floods in the lagoon.
The dynasty's envoys to the steppe tribes did not return.

notes: Probe: 'dominant naval power' 0.42, 'supremacy' 0.45, 'market leader' 0.22; 'garden city' 0.83, 'world city' 0.42, 'network strategy' 0.45, 'sponge city' 0.10, ordinary 'city' 0.01. I could not find one pattern joining the dominance words and the planning 'city', so the label is a list and the test covers the dominance half.
